To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glyA gene of M. extoquens AM1, which encodes serine hydroxylmethyltransferase (glyA), was cloned and sequenced and that the gene was inactivated to produce an SHMT null strain that was unable to grow on C2 compounds as well as on methanol.
we have cloned and inactivated glyA, the structural gene of serine hydroxylmethyltransferase, one of the key genes in the serine cycle.

the gene encoding serine hydroxy-methyltransferase (glyA) was isolated from the genome of M. extornquens AM1, the enzyme was shown to be involved in C1 and C2 assimilation, and the gene was shown to be not linked to the serine cycle genes previously described.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic analysis of the serine pathway for C1 assimilating by Methylobacteriurn extorquens.
the genetic analysis of the serine pathway for C1 assimilating in M. extorqunens AM1.
the genetic organization of the serine pathway in M. extorqunens AM1, which is a model organism for the study of C1 metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serine cycle of M. extonquens AM1 is composed of at least five genes, and that the serine hydroxylmethyltransferase gene, glyA, is the last one to be identified.
the serine cycle is the only pathway for C1 assimilating in M. extorques AM1.
the serine cycle genes in M. extorq uens AM1 are not clustered but scattered in four regions of the chromosome.

the serine cycle genes are scattered over the genome of M. extornquens AM1.
the serine cycle of M. extoronquens AM1 consists of at least five different genetic loci.

SHMT is essential for C2 assimilation in M. extorqens, and the serine cycle may be a major pathway for C2 assimilaton in M. extoquens AM1.
the serine cycle, which was believed to be the sole pathway for C1 assimilatory metabolism in M. extorqunens AM1, is not the only pathway for this metabolism in this strain.
